proposals.premise: Friday’s muddy north rows make a plain harvest note the clearest basis for a friendly, current visit plan.
proposals.opening: Desktop shows the note beside the straw basket photo; phone shows the note first. Hours, last slot, and shop access share the same view.
proposals.move: The first control is a picking-time selector. Choosing a Saturday slot reserves it, with confirmation appearing directly below; shop-only visitors continue without booking.
proposals.tradeoff: This gains immediate clarity and an informal tone, but gives the hand-marked map less initial visual prominence.

proposals.premise: The hand-marked map can turn today’s access limits into orientation: Ashmead and Russet rows open, north rows muddy, gravel path usable.
proposals.opening: Desktop opens with the map beside Saturday details; phone stacks the map above them. The basket photo shares space with the shop-without-booking message.
proposals.move: The first control is a Saturday slot button. Selecting a time reserves picking and places confirmation beneath the map, while the gravel shop route remains visible.
proposals.tradeoff: This gains spatial confidence before arrival, but visitors must read map markings carefully to distinguish picking access from shop access.
